fire: The survey separates two ideas: job security (can you be fired?) and job satisfaction (do you like the work?).
Engineers distinguish between static load (what rests on the beam?) and dynamic load (what moves across it?).
We track two numbers: customer retention (who stays?) and customer acquisition (who joins?).
The framework has two axes: market concentration (how many firms compete?) and vertical integration (who owns the suppliers?).
Teachers assess both reading fluency (how fast can you read?) and reading comprehension (how much do you understand?).
There are two questions here: technical feasibility (can it be built?) and commercial viability (will anyone buy it?).
Ecologists measure species richness (how many kinds are there?) and species evenness (how balanced are their numbers?).
The audit looks at data accuracy (are the values right?) and data completeness (is anything missing?).
